input: Strings contain only ASCII characters U+0000 through U+007F, so Python code-point and JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit indexing agree. Arbitrary Unicode and boxed strings are outside the paired domain. s has length n in [0, 4294967295], and k is a positive integer in [1, 4294967295]. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: An immutable string formed by reversing the first k characters of every consecutive block of 2*k characters, leaving the second half unchanged. A final block shorter than k is fully reversed; a final block from k through 2*k - 1 reverses only its first k. Empty input returns the empty string.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Swaps affect only a freshly materialized character sequence. The result string is immutable; equal-string object identity is not part of the contract.
numeric: 2*k, start + k and each final start increment are at most 12884901885, well within the safe-integer range. Indices and endpoint sentinels are exact integers. No bitwise truncation or input-code-point arithmetic is used.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(n + 1) auxiliary character storage, plus O(n + 1) returned-string storage. Materialization and final join are charged even if k = 1. Each character participates in at most one swap and each block uses a single inward two-pointer pass.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 440 UTF-8 bytes, including the Solution class, method signature, every loop, condition, allocation, standard built-in call, annotation/comment where present, whitespace and terminal newline. There are no custom helper definitions, imports, generated implementations or hidden source expansion. Built-in operations are not free: their allocations and work are included in the stated runtime/storage costs. TreeNode, where used, is an explicit caller-owned input shape and no node is constructed. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source; method-style interface parity with frozen sources remains unqualified.
